text.name: motor_metadata_policy
text.data: Only actuator ctrlrange/forcerange impose the listed torque caps. Rated/no-load speeds, electrical data and internal ratios are descriptive metadata. Gear remains 1 because torque inputs are joint-side. Do not multiply output torque by internal ratio again. Additional transmissions and actual supplies remain uncalibrated. M3508 P19 values are catalogue references for a CAD wheel assembly with a custom gearbox. Peak duration, thermal derating, efficiency, friction and rotor inertia are not modeled. RH-17 ideal brakes are modeled by joint equalities; calibrated brake holding torque, electrical dynamics and delays are not modeled. brake_present: 1=confirmed, 0=absent, -1=not documented.

text.name: motor_DM4340P_unresolved

text.name: RH17_brake_policy
text.data: Two ideal joint-equality brakes, brake_body_rear_fold and brake_body_front_fold, default ENGAGED. polycoef[0]=0 holds qpos0. Before engaging at another angle set model.eq_data[id,0]=q-qpos0 and data.eq_active[id]=True. Release with data.eq_active[id]=False. RH-17 motors use actuator group 1, disabled by default via option actuatorgroupdisable=1. When both brakes release, clear bit (1<<1) in model.opt.disableactuator; when both engage set that bit. Motor torque limits do not limit brake reaction; finite holding torque and engagement delays are uncalibrated. find_angle.py B toggles both brakes; startup and reset engage at the initial pose.

text.name: thigh_inertial_policy
text.data: Each thigh structural group (upper_leg frame + knee_crank + pushrod with bearings) totals 0.300 kg; drive mass remains in its 2 kg hip. All original visuals and inertials are retained, with simplified collision envelopes on external structures. The inner crank and pushrod retain their own collision outlines, joints, inertia and visual motion. Inertial provenance: leg_inertial_sources.json.

text.name: hip_inertial_policy
text.data: All four hips are 2 kg each per mechanical/user instruction, representing three DM6248P motors and mounting hardware. COM is at the hip motor housing geometric center in the user-indicated image region. Central inertia uses the CAD aggregate tensor scaled to 2 kg and retained as an estimate when relocating the equivalent lump. Both base_link and body_front exclude their two chassis-mounted motor inertials to avoid duplicate mass. No independent thigh_drive COM. CAD sources were verified by hashes; no new SolidWorks export or measured COM/inertia is claimed.

text.name: hip_motor_lumping_policy
text.data: Four 2 kg hip modules, front and rear. All 12 DM6248P visual meshes are retained; collision uses fitted housing envelopes. Drive visual geometry remains under ordinary bodies; no thigh_drive body inertials. Kinematics and 0.300 kg thigh structural totals are preserved.

text.name: rl_collision_policy
text.data: Separate RL model generated from p1_reconfigurable.xml. CAD-fitted primitives and low-vertex convex envelopes replace 332 part-level collision geoms. All visual geoms, body inertials, joints, actuators and brake equalities are preserved. Moving crank/pushrod outlines are included; frame-pushrod and pushrod-shank contact exclusions represent connected four-bar assembly clearances. Drive housings and other non-parent robot bodies have self-contact enabled. Folding side plates, RH-17 housings and folding couplers share assembly bit 8 and ignore each other because their CAD envelopes overlap in the assembled chassis; they still contact legs, arms, main plates, other drive housings and terrain. Normal robot geoms use contype=1/conaffinity=11; folding assembly uses 8/3; ground uses 2/9. Parent-body filtering remains enabled. No Python collision callback is required. Wheel tires are analytic cylinders fitted about their actual spin axes; separate hubs retain axial protrusions. Legs, side plates, linkage and segmented claws use ordinary file-based STL collision meshes for viewer compatibility. Import the XML together with its complete meshes directory. This is a locomotion/reconfiguration collision approximation, not a detailed movable-finger grasp model.
